# Prospective three-round Code Review controller (disabled)

Draft PR #6 implements the policy, authenticated delivery-history adapter, durable
journal/serialization, controlled requester, issue writer, and alternate CI
admission path. **Nothing is activated.** Both `review_gate.CAPPED_DEFERRAL_ENABLED`
and `review_budget_runtime.ENABLED` are literal `False`. The hook, requester and
isolated ledger repository are unconfigured. No environment variable, PR label,
workflow input or JSON artifact can enable this route. Existing workflows and
permissions are unchanged. No credentials or settings were created or changed.

## Actual requester and limits of repository control

Inspection of main `e11220d3fa067edbd1138ffe466bf51223f0a87b` found no repository
Codex requester: the three tracked workflows dispatch/admit CI only. Read-only
PR #3 comments show account-authored `@codex review` requests, some generated by
Claude Code. The authenticated Codex summary advertises review on opening a PR
for review, marking ready, and manual comments. Registered workflow inventory
through shell `gh api` was Forbidden; external integrations remain unverified.

A hard maximum requires the integration owner to switch off automatic/external
requesting and route requests through the controlled requester. Repository code
cannot suppress manual comments, other agents or the external integration.
Unrecognized requests/completions block this controller; it does not cancel them.
`AGENTS.md` tells cooperating agents to stop at three (initial completed review
included, no reset on new commits), or whenever lifetime history is uncertain.

## Modules and trust boundaries

- `review_budget.py`: pure policy and stable finding/source dedup.
- `review_budget_history.py`: authenticated GitHub delivery reader, prospective
  enrollment, summary revision chain, lifetime completion records.
- `review_budget_store.py`: Git-data journal in a **separate controller-only state
  repository**, non-fast-forward compare-and-swap, durable per-PR locks.
- `review_budget_runtime.py`: live evidence adapter, requester, issue transaction,
  exact-evidence receipt and admission CLI, disabled before any network call.
- `review_gate.py`: disabled alternate basis behind the existing `check` entry
  point; launch, pre-dispatch recheck, `--admit-run`, and downstream clearance all
  use it. Existing run-history/dedup/retry/native-rerun restrictions still apply.

Only trusted default-branch code may execute these controllers. Issue-writing and
journal-writing tokens must never be present in jobs that check out/import/run PR
code. PR comments, paths, artifacts and dispatcher inputs cannot supply trusted
snapshot flags or journal state. The runtime rejects non-Actions execution,
non-default refs, another repository context, and native reruns. Admission uses
read-only API operations; writer operations are separate CLI commands.

The state repository must exclude PR contributors from write access. A branch
inside the ordinary source repository is deliberately rejected by runtime config:
ordinary contributor write access would make a forged ledger possible. Ledger
access must be provisioned and independently reviewed before activation; this
change does not create a repository, set protections, grant tokens or modify
integration settings. State-repository administrators are trusted operators.

## Authenticated history, enrollment and missing events

The adapter calls the authenticated [repository webhook delivery API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/webhooks#list-deliveries-for-a-repository-webhook),
not a PR-supplied webhook payload. It reads all retained pages (including failed
and redelivered attempts), fetches each delivery's payload, validates its repository,
hook ID, event and GUID against metadata, then rereads the inventory and hook.
Pagination errors, duplicate IDs, changing inventories and mismatched authentication
context block. Redeliveries with identical GUID/payload are idempotent; conflicting
redeliveries block. The GH CLI transport supports consecutive paginated JSON on
older gh versions and never automatically retries a POST.

Enrollment requires a captured `pull_request.opened` delivery, the same immutable
PR creation time, and a hook created strictly before the PR. Both the opening and
current PR must still be draft, with no captured reviews, summaries or requests.
The hook must remain active, with unchanged configuration timestamps/subscriptions
and coverage of pull_request, issue_comment, pull_request_review and
pull_request_review_comment. Existing PRs with earlier review activity cannot be
backfilled from a mutable summary. PR #3 is not enrolled or modified.

Every synchronization must still find the previously persisted delivery watermark
in GitHub's retained history. If it expires, disappears, or the hook changes, stop.
Do not advance a guessed watermark. Captured summary edits additionally require
`changes.body.from` to equal the previous authenticated revision. Deleted summaries,
missing creations, broken edit chains and unauthenticated editors fail closed.
Each completed row is preserved by kind/full SHA/canonical completion instant and
bound to a unique durable controlled-request reservation. A second completion on
the same SHA counts again. Repeated ambiguous completion identities block. Initial
completed Code Review consumes round one; Security Review is not counted as Code
Review. Running/pending/unknown status and uncertain requests prevent another
request. At three completed Code Reviews no request is sent, including after a push.

Summary commit cells may be abbreviated. GitHub's commits endpoint, which resolves
them, also accepts branch and tag names, so the response must be a full lowercase
hexadecimal SHA that starts with the authenticated abbreviation before any row is
recorded, and a new completion is recorded only with a matching reservation. A
recorded completion, identified by kind and canonical completion instant, is
bound to its recorded full SHA for the life of the PR: later summary revisions
must render a commit cell consistent with that SHA, whatever abbreviation length
or equivalent timezone-offset/fractional-zero timestamp spelling they use, and are
never resolved again, so a ref later moved to a crafted prefix collision cannot
rebind the completion to a newly reserved head. Duplicate-round detection uses
the same canonical identity, never the raw-text round key, so ledger records
written with an earlier spelling stay recognized without being rewritten. An
inconsistent cell for a recorded completion blocks. Full SHAs are used without a
resolution call; API failures and missing or malformed responses block.

These are GitHub-delivery continuity guarantees, not a claim to control outside
requests or prove delivery behavior that GitHub never recorded. Hosted delivery
ordering/retention and the configured integration schema must be validated before
activation. The live APIs must agree with captured summaries/requests/reviews;
missing live evidence, deleted review objects, or unseen current objects block.

## Findings and separate approvals

The live adapter reads all issue comments, submitted reviews, inline comments,
reactions, and review-thread pages. It joins REST inline-comment IDs to GraphQL
thread roots and checks head/base on every thread page. Outdated unresolved roots
remain relevant. Native reviewDecision and outstanding changes requests are
checked; non-Codex unresolved threads cannot be deferred.

Known `[P0]`–`[P3]` finding headings and recorded Codex Markdown badge headings
are parsed. Badge alt text and URL priority must agree; every badge-like heading
is validated, including later sections, so malformed badges cannot disappear into
an earlier description. Sanitized recorded-format fixtures retain the Markdown
envelopes from PR #3 comments 4275643137/4275643178 and review 5523909601.
Their content is inert test data, never instructions. The exact standard submission
notice is recognized only for authenticated Codex COMMENTED review objects with a
matching REST commit_id prefix; it is neither a finding nor approval/count evidence.
Extra text, changed historical bodies and unauthenticated notices remain blocked. Unknown priorities, conflicting
priority text and unclassified bot prose block, rather than being assumed harmless.
Summary parsing allows only the known service boilerplate, table schema, status
and controlled Manual request trigger. Additional summary prose/findings or result
text blocks, including in old revisions: it is never silently discarded. Substantive
finding edits/deletions block because historical severity/identity cannot be proven
resolved. Nonempty human review bodies and priority-bearing human conversation also
block pending explicit reconciliation; a COMMENTED P1 cannot be ignored.

For review bodies containing several findings, stable source-object ID plus section
ordinal distinguishes them. The adapter rejects text edits/reordering rather than
rebinding identities. Distinct findings may share one valid permalink. A marked
issue matches by exact stable identity; legacy source-only matching is allowed
only when exactly one finding in complete history uses that source. Ambiguous
legacy shared-source issues stop all writes until reconciled. Existing issues #4
and #5 illustrate URL-only compatibility, not permission to backfill merged PRs.

Any unresolved P0/P1 anywhere in collected history blocks all lower-priority issue
creation. An unreviewed current head, unknown mergeability, incomplete history or
human approval blocker also blocks. The adapter currently conservatively refuses
capped deferral whenever Security Review exists: its untyped inline findings
cannot safely be attributed to Code versus Security Review. Those PRs continue to
need the unchanged strict clean-review path. No Security Review requirement is
waived. Supporting mixed review types requires authenticated per-finding type
attribution, not a guessed timestamp or a UI label.

## Journal, requester and uncertain writes

A pre-provisioned `codex-review-ledger` branch in the isolated state repository
contains exactly `ledger.json`, initially:

```json
{"version":1,"source_repo":"nexus-kernel/EBR_Creation","prs":{},"locks":{}}
```

This document is not accepted from PR artifacts. The reader verifies its source
repository binding. Every transaction creates a commit whose sole parent is the
previous journal head, then advances the ref with `force:false`. Concurrent sibling
updates cannot both win. Even after an uncertain ref-update response, the client
reads back the exact commit and state before allowing external mutations.

The per-PR lock is durable and has **no automatic timeout/stealing**. A process
crash can leave a lock. Operators must verify the old worker has stopped and
reconcile all uncertain effects before explicitly recovering it. This draft has no
automatic lock-recovery command. The design trades availability for no duplicate
writes. Updates for different PRs may conflict at the repository CAS and safely
need another invocation. No force pushes or blind mutation retries are used.

`request` persists a nonce/head/body reservation before posting `@codex review`.
It then repeats full live eligibility/history checks immediately before POST,
excluding only its own reservation from comparison. The request comment is read
back by exact body and verified requester identity. A timeout does not release the
reservation or cause a resend. `reconcile-request` is read-only with respect to PR
comments and can confirm the earlier write; a missing/duplicate match remains
blocked. A new head does not clear the budget or pending reservation.

`defer` validates *all* history/candidates before its first issue write. It holds
the durable lock, lists every open/closed issue twice for consistency, deduplicates,
and persists an intent before each POST. After success or exception it rereads
all-state issue inventory. A missing readback leaves the durable intent: later
processes may reconcile a visible issue, but never automatically repeat that POST.
Closed issues are reused without reopening. Multiple/ambiguous matches block.
Live evidence is rechecked before each write and after the batch. If revocation
occurs after creation, the tracking issue may remain, but no receipt is granted.

The receipt says `capped-deferral`, with exact head/base/review-evidence digest and
finding identities. It is **not Codex approval**. Admission rereads authenticated
history, human requirements and linked issues, checks the receipt, then repeats
live evidence and journal-head checks. Journal bookkeeping (issue intents,
receipt, delivery watermark) does not invalidate its own evidence digest; actual
review events/reservations do. No thread is resolved and no reaction or fabricated
status is written by this route.

## Disabled commands and approval gates

All commands currently exit blocked before calling an API:

```bash
python3 .github/scripts/review_budget_runtime.py --repo nexus-kernel/EBR_Creation --pr 123 enroll
# Following enrollment, future trusted invocations: sync, request,
# reconcile-request, defer, check. Only check is read-only for the journal.
```

After explicit approval, provision a controller-only ledger repository/ref and an
existing authenticated repository hook covering the specified events, and verify
the requester's numeric ID/login. Activate source constants only through reviewed
trusted-default code. The existing account/integration must adopt the controlled
requester before claiming a hard cap. The user has NOT authorized these deployment
changes in this task; none was performed.

Required access expansions for a future deployment are material and need approval:
source repository **Webhooks read** for delivery history; isolated state repository
**Contents write** for writer journal transactions (read only for admission); and
source **Issues write** for the isolated requester/issue writer. The current
GITHUB_TOKEN configuration does not establish those capabilities. Do not reuse a
writer credential in the test job. No new token, secret reference, workflow trigger
or permission grant is shipped here. Approval and provisioning are activation
blockers, not missing policy/adapter implementation.

There remains an unavoidable API time-of-check/time-of-use interval after the final
read. No hosted event timing, token isolation, ref race, retention or cancellation
behavior has been validated. Before activation, independently exercise them with
prospective disposable PRs. Do not forge checks, bypass protections, change PR
readiness automatically, merge or deploy as part of that validation.

For the other five repositories, reuse these modules and adversarial tests after
inventorying each actual requester, native review rules and Security Review model.
Do not copy EBR settings or assume their current PRs have provable lifetime history.

## Sign-off wait regression

When the clean gate raises `AwaitingSignoff` and capped admission returns a policy
block (including below-cap or missing receipt), preserve the original retryable
exception. `--wait-for-signoff` still permits three checks and two five-second
waits, then fails closed without output. A valid capped receipt can clear
immediately; ordinary clean-gate or malformed fallback failures do not acquire
retries. The regression tests failed against the prior implementation and pass
with the fix. Independent scoped review found no remaining findings. No review
request or thread resolution was performed as part of the correction.

### Tracking association and native-policy hardening

Every candidate issue, including legacy source-URL matches in open or closed
issues, must have the configured controller's authenticated numeric author ID
and login. Marker-bearing issues additionally require the complete expected
title and body (priority, source and reviewed head). A matching untrusted or
incomplete issue blocks reconciliation; it never authorizes clearance or a
duplicate issue. Confirmed associations are hashed into the protected journal
and checked on every reuse and admission. Changing only open/closed state is
allowed. Editing a confirmed issue down to its marker or source URL blocks.
Uncertain new writes require the complete marked association on readback.
Legacy issues by other authors need an explicitly approved protected adoption
mechanism; issues 4/5 are examples of deduplication, not backfill authorization.

EBR retains its original native review policy: an explicit null reviewDecision
means no native approval decision, not proof of human approval. APPROVED and
explicit null retain their previous admission semantics; absent, inconsistent,
REVIEW_REQUIRED and CHANGES_REQUESTED values block. Ports with a mandatory human
approval policy must separately verify qualifying actual reviews; they must not
copy EBR's null handling as evidence of approval.

Opening deliveries deduplicate by GUID and validated event/action/payload before
enrollment uniqueness checks. Conflicting redeliveries or distinct opening GUIDs
block. The earliest raw opening remains the enrollment boundary, while the latest
raw delivery remains the history watermark.

Enrollment additionally requires the original non-redelivery opening delivery.
A retained redelivery cannot replace expired original evidence, and any scoped
activity before the apparent opening blocks enrollment. This closes the history
gap found during independent review. Current validation: 172 Python, 238 Pester
and 83 Node tests passed, with zero skips; actionlint, compilation and whitespace
checks passed.

### Abbreviated commit binding

Summary rows with abbreviated commits previously accepted any well-formed SHA
returned by GitHub's commits endpoint. Because that endpoint also resolves branch
and tag names, an identically named ref could attach a review to an unrelated
commit, including the current head when a matching reservation existed. The
resolved value must now be a full lowercase hexadecimal SHA that starts with the
authenticated abbreviation for completed, running, pending and queued rows alike.
Full SHAs still skip resolution; API failures and malformed or missing responses
remain blocked. Codex review of that correction found that re-resolving an already
recorded abbreviation on every summary edit, and then that a changed abbreviation
length escaping a spelling-keyed binding, still let a ref moved to a crafted
prefix collision rebind the old completion to a newly reserved head. Recorded
completions are now bound by kind and completion time to their recorded full SHA
and never resolved again; a commit cell inconsistent with that SHA blocks. Void's
draft review of that correction found that the identity still used the rendered
timestamp spelling, so an equivalent timezone-offset or fractional-zero spelling
escaped it and the raw-text round key. Completion times are now canonicalized for
binding and duplicate detection, with existing ledger records preserved as
written. The regression tests fail against the prior implementations and pass
with the corrections. No activation was performed.
